name: Boorong (Aboriginal Australian) sky
summary: Stars of the Boorong people who lived by Lake Tyrrell in southeastern Australia: kangaroo, eagle, crow, cockatoo and boomerang in the sky.

Wjl.name: The Long-Necked Turtle
Wjl.description: Pollux and the neighbouring stars of Gemini.

Yur.name: The Fan-Tailed Cockatoo
Yur.description: Castor and the neighbouring stars of Gemini.

Kul.name: The Two Teenage Boys
Kul.description: Orion’s Belt and Sword with the fainter surrounding stars.

Lnk.name: The Girls
Lnk.description: The Pleiades: a group of young girls.

Pur.name: The Red Kangaroo
Pur.description: The bright Capella and the neighbouring stars of Auriga and Perseus.

Bun.name: The Ringtail Possum
Bun.description: The stars of the Southern Cross, with the star at the tip of the cross. Not visible from Hungary.

Djt.name: The Red-Tailed Parrot
Djt.description: The reddish Antares and the head of Scorpius.

War.name: The Crow
War.description: The bright Canopus and its surroundings. Not visible from Hungary.

Cwr.name: The Female Crow, War’s Wife
Cwr.description: Eta Carinae and the stars of Carina. Not visible from Hungary.

Ydk.name: The Australian Owlet-Nightjar
Ydk.description: Achernar and its surroundings. Not visible from Hungary.

Tbg.name: The Hakea Bush and the Fan-Tailed Birds

Bbg.name: The Red-Kneed Dotterel
Bbg.description: Alpha Centauri and the stars of Circinus. Not visible from Hungary.

Krk.name: The Australian Kestrel
Krk.description: The end of the tail of Scorpius; the name also means a spear-thrower. From Hungary it is visible only near the southern horizon.

Nln.name: The Malleefowl
Nln.description: The constellation Lyra with the bright Vega. The malleefowl builds a nest mound in which it incubates its eggs.

Unu.name: The Lizard
Unu.description: The stars of Canis Major below Sirius (the lizard is Sigma Canis Majoris).

Ktc.name: The Pair of Brolgas
Ktc.description: The stars around the Magellanic Clouds: a male and a female brolga. Not visible from Hungary.

Wpl.name: The Wedge-Tailed Eagle
Wpl.description: The bright Sirius and its neighbours.

Cwp.name: The Female Eagle, Warepil’s Wife
Cwp.description: The bright Rigel and Lepus, and the neighbouring stars of Eridanus.

Tot.name: The Purple-Crowned Lorikeet
Tot.description: The bright Altair and the stars of Aquila.

Mar.name: The Meat Ant
Mar.description: The bright Arcturus. According to tradition, it showed people the larvae of the wood ant (bittur), a favourite food; its appearance in the evening sky marked the time of gathering.

Wrn.name: The Milky Way
Wrn.description: The name of the Milky Way; here it is marked by a star of Sagittarius where the Milky Way is brightest.

Wkr.name: The Singing Bushlark
Wkr.description: A star in Boötes, west of Arcturus.

Col.name: The Ant
Col.description: The double star in the head of Capricornus.

Won.name: The Boomerang
Won.description: The arc of Corona Australis. From Hungary it would be visible only at the very edge of the horizon, extremely low.

Min.name: The Maned Snake
Min.description: Part of the Milky Way in the constellation Vela. Not visible from Hungary.
